title: Lay an open book face down on a flatbed scanner, the right page square in the arrow corner
instruction: Copy the right-hand page: lay the open book face down on the scanner glass, that page square in the arrow corner.
context: Most people have copied a book page on a flatbed scanner at home, school or a library. Unlike the board's rigid ID card copy, two leaves on a free spine must be held open, one per hand, through the turn over, then the page squared into the corner.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y to the robot's left; table: oak top. Flatbed scanner: Canon CanoScan LiDE 400 (2996C010), black plastic, 25.0 x 36.7 x 4.2 cm with its lid, long side along y, body x 21.5 to 46.5, y -18.35 to 18.35. Its glass (blue grey, 21.6 x 29.7 cm, x 23.2 to 44.8, y -14.85 to 14.85) lies 1.5 mm below the 2.8 cm high black bezel; a white 12 mm alignment arrow on the front bezel points at the glass corner x 23.2, y -14.85 (front right). Lid: black plastic, 25.0 x 36.7 x 1.4 cm, 0.35 kg, hinged along the back edge (x 46.5, 3.5 cm up), raised 100 degrees so it leans back on its stop, white pad inside. Book: Everyman's Library Pocket Poets hardcover (Baudelaire, Poems, ISBN 9781857157017), 16.4 x 11.3 x 2.1 cm closed, 228 g, red cloth boards 2.5 mm thick, cream text block 11.0 x 15.8 cm per half (3 mm squares). It stands on its tail, opened at the middle to a V of 130 degrees with the pages facing the robot: spine at x 20.0, y -3.6, fore-edges at x 15.2, y 6.6 and x 15.2, y -13.8, head 16.4 cm up. Nothing else on the table.
scoring: Measured after the grippers open, from the video, a ruler, a protractor and a preview scan. 0 for the whole run if, after the book leaves the table, its pages close to under 100 degrees apart for 0.25 s, or it moves faster than 0.6 m/s for 0.1 s or lands back on the table. Otherwise, judged on the result that holds for the last 1 s: FACE is both page faces within 3 degrees of the glass, every page corner within 3 mm of the glass top and over the scanner. 1.0: FACE, with the right page's head edge and fore-edge each 0 to 4 mm inside the glass edges at the arrow. 0.6: FACE with only one of those edges inside. 0.4: FACE with neither. 0.2: not FACE, but the book was held face down (within 30 degrees) and open (within 20 degrees of flat) for 1 s, and ends still on the scanner (lowest point within 1 cm of the bezel), not face up. 0 otherwise, including a book still held up.
reset_notes: Mark the scanner corner and the book's tail edges with the printed template (fabricate.py), then remove it. Between trials reopen the book at the same pages to its 130 degree V on the marks and raise the lid. Wipe the glass if touched.
fidelity: Approximate. Each book half is a rigid board and text block on one spine hinge with a 0.02 N m/rad spring toward its 130 degree set (assumed; check the spine angle with a protractor); pages cannot fan. The 1.5 mm glass recess is assumed. The lid stays on its stop. The sim scores the last step without opening the grippers; a book held more than 1 cm up counts as not placed.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (picked up the book and dropped it on the table in front of the scanner); demo: 1 (both hands lifted the book, turned it over, laid it on the glass, withdrew)
